title: Dispatch CUS 5: Child Hurt as Two Houses Shift on the Same Plot
summary: A minor injury gives urgency to the dispute over the north ward.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: A kitchen floor at 12 Fenwick Lane moved against the ceiling of a North Loom Street storeroom yesterday morning. Ten-year-old Elsie Hume fell while carrying a kettle and injured her wrist. Inspector Voss reports that no one was crushed and the buildings have since been shored on both sides.

The child is the niece of Beatrice Hume, the visiting registrar. Her family’s home has stood on Fenwick Lane for thirty years by their records. The storeroom below belongs to a cooper who has worked there equally long by his. Both hold valid deeds within their respective cities.

Dr. Saye examined the census volumes beside the shifting wall. When Miss Morrow wrote “disputed address” against the plot in pencil, the pressure on the braces lessened. Miss Hume made an equivalent note in her own book, and the two rooms separated enough for the workmen to check their supports.

The relief lasted until evening. Each city’s rate book still treats the other arrangement as a trespass. Dr. Saye thinks the conflicting entries are drawing the two maps into the same physical account. She urges the councils to record the other households as real without assigning them Alderwick’s existing plots.

Mr. Keene visited Ada Keene to bring medicine for the injured child. She told him her daughter had asked why he resembles the man in the family photographs. He said he did not know how to explain that she resembles someone he has missed for nine years.
